statements.text: The Prime Minister told the Commons that the UK assesses the RAF Fairford incident as highly likely to have been coordinated in Iran and almost certainly directed by the Islamic Revolutionary Guard. He said the government will crack down on Iran's use of criminal networks and bring further sanctions to restrict Iran and the IRGC.

The Prime Minister welcomed President Trump's announcement of a reciprocal energy ceasefire. He said President Zelenskyy has assured him Ukraine would immediately implement it once a start date is confirmed.

Prime Minister Andy Burnham said that support for Ukraine is vital for keeping the UK safe, that the UK is with Ukraine for as long as it takes, and that further support is necessary. He said Russia's aggression cannot be allowed to succeed on the continent.

The Prime Minister has asked Ministers to draw up further sanctions, military and fiscal packages to provide urgent support to Ukraine in the coming weeks, and to accelerate delivery of critical air defence missiles.

At the meeting with President Zelenskyy on 14 October, the leaders said Russia had no interest in peace. The Prime Minister set out the UK's latest package of Lightweight Multirole Missiles, said the UK would keep developing military solutions including retrofitting British capability onto gifted equipment, said the UK would accelerate defensive support ahead of winter on long-range missiles, and said it would continue diplomatic efforts on defensive equipment.

The UK will accelerate deliveries of Lightweight Multirole Missiles, which it says have proven extremely effective against jet-powered drones. It has already committed £1.6 billion to deliver more than 5,000 of them to Ukraine over four years, and will accelerate £10 million of the £45 million missile package to meet Ukraine's most urgent winter needs.

The Prime Minister said the government has announced new funding to help Ukraine get through its fifth winter under Russian bombardment, and a new sanctions package that brings over 90% of Russia's oil producing capacity under UK sanctions.

speakers: Chancellor of the Exchequer John Healey
statements.text: Chancellor John Healey will urge partners at the IMF meetings in Bangkok to fully implement an equivalent ban on Russian LNG. He said he urges partners to back the ban, to curtail the war chest funding Putin.

The Prime Minister confirmed the UK-EU summit will take place in Brussels on 20 November. On the table are a food and drink trade deal, progress on emissions trading and linking energy systems, a youth experience scheme and deeper cooperation on immigration. The trade deal on food and drink is estimated to add over £10 billion a year to the UK economy by 2040.

The Prime Minister said he believes the UK's chances at the summit would be enhanced by being open to discussing the longer-term relationship with the EU. He said his immediate priority is a successful summit outcome, and that he then believes a serious dialogue on long-term options should be set up.

The UK has decided to send air defence and a Voyager aircraft to Saudi Arabia for air-to-air refuelling support. The Prime Minister said a Voyager has already completed 14 operational missions, and condemned the attacks on King Khalid International Airport.

The Prime Minister said he raised the Falkland Islands with President Trump, including the clear and declared will of the islanders to remain British, and said the UK will always do whatever it takes to uphold it.

The Prime Minister said he and Chancellor Merz agreed a new partnership to tackle Russian hybrid threats in Berlin. He confirmed the commitment to establish a new National Centre for Information Defence.
The Prime Minister said the UK will take up the G20 presidency in 2027 and place AI centre stage, capturing its opportunities while guarding against its risks.

Andy Burnham said he is making an offer to the Scottish Government. Douglas Alexander said the Prime Minister's offer to the Scottish Government is a genuine one, and the Scotland Office is ready to work alongside it.

In his speech in Motherwell on 16 October, the Prime Minister made a serious and genuine offer to the Scottish Government. It proposes designing a new model of regional economic empowerment across Scotland, and an offer of DWP devolution for localised employment support. He said the National Economic Council is to meet the First Ministers of Scotland, Wales and Northern Ireland in a couple of weeks to put the offer on the table.

Great British Railways' new headquarters will be built at Becketwell in Derby, with construction expected to begin in early 2027 and be completed by spring 2029. It will accommodate up to 450 GBR staff and is estimated to bring a £151 million boost to Derby's economy.
Heidi Alexander said the biggest shake-up to the railways in a generation is underway, and that she is delighted Becketwell will become GBR's new home.
Pat McFadden said the foundation apprenticeship is part of a £2.5 billion youth employment support package creating up to 500,000 opportunities for young people to earn or learn.
The King has appointed William James Baxter QPM DL as Lord-Lieutenant of County Tyrone, succeeding Sir Robert William Lowry Scott following his retirement on 17 June 2026.
